v.why: Smaller batches give many more Adam updates per epoch, which rescues low-LR underfitting within 243 epochs, though the extra gradient noise could also hurt.
Noisy batch-4 to 10 gradients combined with large Adam steps push runs toward divergence, although the noise could instead act as a helpful regularizer.
The optimal LR shrinks with width, so widening at an already high LR overshoots, though wider nets can also be more robust through averaging.
Large batches give few updates, and wider nets extract more progress per step, but wide nets could also overfit with less gradient noise.
Depth 3 already supplies capacity and widening adds optimization difficulty and overfitting, though more width could also ease deep-net training.
Narrow nets have no spare capacity, so stronger L2 causes underfitting, although a regularized small net could generalize better.
With small batches there are many more steps per epoch, so cumulative L2 shrinkage is larger and strong alpha over-shrinks, though noisy small-batch runs might benefit from the extra damping.
Over-parameterized wide nets overfit and benefit from stronger weight decay, though they might be too redundant for alpha to matter.
Deeper nets train more slowly at tiny LR and stay undertrained in 243 epochs, though added layers could speed feature formation.
Many noisy small-batch updates compensate for the harder optimization of deeper nets, although the noise could instead destabilize them.
Depth substitutes for missing width in narrow nets, while in wide nets the extra layers are redundant.
Strong L2 compounds across more layers and shrinks the signal, though it might also stabilize deeper nets.
Large batches take few steps and have low gradient noise, so a higher LR is needed and tolerated, although a high LR could still overshoot.
Wide nets need a smaller LR because the effective step grows with width, so raising LR destabilizes them, though wide nets might also tolerate it through averaging.
Depth-3 nets have compounding sensitivity to large steps, so a higher LR risks divergence, although it could also speed up their slow training.
A shallow net has little optimization instability to tame, so a lower LR mostly causes undertraining, although it may reduce noise for the final fit.
Larger batches mean fewer steps and less cumulative shrinkage, so they offset the over-regularization from strong alpha, although they could also reduce the benefit of the noise.
A one-layer net relies on width for capacity, while deeper nets can compensate for narrowing, although small tabular tasks may not need the width.
At two layers, weak L2 lets the net use full capacity without the compounded shrinkage of deeper nets, although removing it could encourage overfitting.
At a moderate LR, larger batches cut the update count and leave the net undertrained, although the smoother gradients might allow cleaner convergence.

raw:
**Eight practitioner assumptions, negated**

1. Smaller batches give noisier, less stable training. If false, small batches at low LR supply the updates that underfitting runs lack, and at high LR they add instability.
2. Wider networks are uniformly safer. If false, wide layers at high LR overshoot because the optimal LR shrinks with width. Wide layers help at large batch because each step does more.
3. Deeper networks have more capacity. If false, depth is a costly substitute for width. It helps narrow nets, while strong L2 or high LR makes it harmful.
4. L2 is a harmless, mild regularizer. If false, strong alpha collapses narrow nets and small-batch runs, where many steps accumulate shrinkage, and helps only over-parameterized wide nets.
5. LR and batch size scale together by the linear/sqrt rule. If false, raising LR at large batch is the real fix, because large-batch runs are step-starved.
6. Depth and LR are independent. If false, deep nets tolerate high LR badly and slow deep nets at low LR undertrain in 243 epochs.
7. Width and depth add capacity. If false, depth 3 flips the sign of width and shallow nets depend on width.
8. Weaker L2 is neutral. If false, removing L2 at moderate depth or high LR changes the optimization conditioning.
